document_check.note: Yoon EJ, Lee J-Y, Kwak S and Kim YK (2023). Mild behavioral impairment linked to progression to Alzheimer's disease and cortical thinning in amnestic mild cognitive impairment. Front. Aging Neurosci. 14:1051621, doi:10.3389/fnagi.2022.1051621, published 4 January 2023. Retrospective clinical cohort of 1,184 amnestic MCI patients from two Seoul centres (2012 to 2020), 284 progressed to AD. The univariate Cox HR for SGDS (1.040, 1.007 to 1.075, p = 0.017) is on page 5 and the SGDS > 6 sensitivity analysis (HR 1.237, 0.850 to 1.798, p = 0.266) is on page 7. This matches the assigned study and result.

cited_result: Association of the baseline short Geriatric Depression Scale (SGDS) score with progression from amnestic MCI to Alzheimer's disease (1,184 patients, 284 progressed, mean follow-up 3.1 years). Principal result appraised: univariate Cox HR 1.040 per SGDS point (95% CI 1.007 to 1.075, p = 0.017). Secondary result: the authors' Discussion sensitivity analysis, in which the affective dysregulation cluster with SGDS > 6 (n = 285) did not differ in risk of progression from the asymptomatic cluster without significant depressive symptoms (n = 326), HR 1.237 (0.850 to 1.798), p = 0.266.
tool_reason: The cited result is the association of one prognostic factor (baseline SGDS score) with a later outcome (progression to AD) estimated by Cox regression, which the authors frame as identifying predictors of progression rather than as a causal exposure effect or the performance of a model, so QUIPS applies.

domains.rationale: Place, period, inclusion and exclusion criteria and the baseline sample are described. The recruitment method (consecutive or not) and the number of aMCI patients screened, eligible or excluded are not reported. Eligibility was conditioned on events after baseline: at least one follow-up and more than one year of follow-up, and exclusion of patients who later progressed to a non-AD dementia. The cohort is therefore a selected set of retained patients whose later course was known, and the SGDS-AD association could differ in the excluded patients (early dropouts, early converters, non-AD progressors).

signalling.question: 1d. Adequate description of the sampling frame and recruitment?
signalling.quote: For this study, inclusion criteria were: (1) 60 to 85 years of age at baseline; (2) at least one follow-up; (3) more than 1 year of a follow-up time; and (4) administration of neuropsychiatric inventory questionnaire (NPI-Q) at their basal visit.

signalling.question: 1e. Adequate description of the period and place of recruitment?
signalling.quote: A total 1,184 individuals with aMCI who visited SMG-SNU Boramae Medical Center or Dongjak-Gu Center for Dementia between 2012 and 2020 were included in the present study.

signalling.question: 1f. Adequate description of inclusion and exclusion criteria (and are they appropriate)?
signalling.quote: Exclusion criteria were: (1) history of head trauma, brain tumor, stroke, intellectual disability, or any severe medical, neurological, or psychiatric illness affecting cognitive function; (2) a history of alcohol or drug abuse; and (3) progression to dementia other than AD such as dementia with Lewy body, vascular dementia, and frontotemporal lobe dementia.

domains.rationale: All 1,184 included patients appear in the analysis (900 stable, 284 progressed), but only because patients without at least one follow-up and more than one year of follow-up were excluded at the eligibility stage. Their number, reasons and characteristics are not reported, so attrition is hidden rather than absent. Stable patients were censored at their last assessment after follow-up ranging from 0.9 to 9.4 years, with no reasons for the end of follow-up and no comparison of those with short and long follow-up.

signalling.quote: During follow-ups, total 284 participants developed AD (24%).

signalling.question: 2b. Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out?

signalling.question: 2c. Reasons for loss to follow-up provided?
signalling.quote: Searched for reasons for the end of follow-up (death, withdrawal, transfer) in the stable group; the only description is: Time from baseline to last assessment for the stable aMCI group and conversion time from aMCI to AD for the aMCI-AD group.

signalling.question: 2d. Adequate description of participants lost to follow-up?
signalling.quote: Searched for the number or characteristics of patients excluded for inadequate follow-up or censored early; none reported.

signalling.question: 2e. No important differences between participants who completed the study and those who did not?
signalling.quote: Searched for a comparison of included patients with those excluded for inadequate follow-up or for progression to a non-AD dementia; none reported.

domains.rationale: The factor is clearly defined (SGDS at baseline, range 0 to 15) and was measured before the outcome, and the principal analysis keeps it continuous. The paper does not say who administered the SGDS or in what form (the instrument list for the clinical psychologists names only the MMSE, CDR and CERAD-K), cites no validation, and does not report how many patients had a missing SGDS score. The > 6 cut-off used for 'significant depressive symptoms' in the sensitivity analysis is not referenced or justified.

domains.rationale: Progression to AD is defined by NINCDS-ADRDA criteria, assessed with the same battery at follow-up and diagnosed at consensus conferences, without biomarker or neuropathological confirmation. Visit intervals varied, so the time of detected progression depends on when patients were seen. There is no statement that the diagnosing clinicians were unaware of baseline depressive symptoms; depressive symptoms can lower cognitive test scores and influence a clinical dementia diagnosis, so misclassification could be related to the prognostic factor.

signalling.question: 4a. A clear definition of the outcome is provided?
signalling.quote: The diagnosis of the AD and aMCI were based on the criteria of the National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Disorders and Stroke and AD and Related Disorders Association (NINCDS-ADRDA) and Petersen’s criteria, respectively (McKhann et al., 1984; Petersen, 2004).

signalling.question: 4b. Method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable?
signalling.quote: Moreover, although we adopted the standardized clinical diagnostic criteria and diagnosis was made at consensus conferences attended by psychiatrists and neuropsychologists, the diagnosis of AD was not confirmed neuropathologically.

signalling.question: 4c. The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants?
signalling.quote: Although we evaluated NPI-Q at every visit during the follow-up period, it was difficult to consider the chronicity of symptoms due to the varying visit interval and follow-up time.

signalling.question: 4d. (Additional) Was the outcome determined without knowledge of the prognostic factor?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods and limitations for any statement that the consensus diagnosis was made blind to baseline SGDS or NPI-Q results; none reported.

domains.rationale: The principal estimate is univariate: it is not adjusted for baseline MMSE, age or education, each of which was itself associated with progression, nor for co-occurring neuropsychiatric symptoms, with which SGDS is strongly associated (asymptomatic cluster 4.5 against 7.8 and 7.3 in the symptomatic clusters). SGDS was entered as a covariate in the multivariable models but its adjusted HR is not reported. APOE genotype and cardiovascular disease were not measured. The sensitivity analysis does not state its adjustment set.

signalling.quote: Other important risk factors of progression to AD, such as APOE genotypes and cardiovascular disease, were not considered for survival analyses.

signalling.question: 5b. Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided?
signalling.quote: A positive family history was defined as one or more first-degree relatives with documented dementia.

signalling.quote: All participants were administered the Korean mini-mental state examination (MMSE), the clinical dementia rating (CDR), and the Consortium to Establish a Registry for AD for Koreans (CERAD-K) neuropsychological battery (Lee et al., 2002) by the trained clinical psychologists at baseline and subsequent follow-ups.

signalling.question: 5d. The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants?
signalling.quote: All participants were administered the Korean mini-mental state examination (MMSE), the clinical dementia rating (CDR), and the Consortium to Establish a Registry for AD for Koreans (CERAD-K) neuropsychological battery (Lee et al., 2002) by the trained clinical psychologists at baseline and subsequent follow-ups.

signalling.question: 5e. Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data?
signalling.quote: Searched the Statistical analysis section for missing covariate data or imputation; none described.

signalling.question: 5f. Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design?
signalling.quote: Two symptomatic groups had higher SGDS scores than the asymptomatic group.

signalling.question: 5g. Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis?
signalling.quote: SGDS scores (HR [95% CI] = 1.040 (1.007–1.075), p = 0.017) were significantly associated with the risk of progression to AD in univariate Cox regression analyses, and were used as covariates in the following Cox multivariate regression analyses.

domains.rationale: The principal univariate HR is reported with its confidence interval, but event counts by SGDS level are not given, the proportional hazards assumption and the linearity of the per-point effect are not reported as checked, and non-AD dementia progressors were excluded rather than handled as competing events. Covariates were chosen by univariable significance and the adjusted SGDS estimate is not reported. The sensitivity analysis appears only in the Discussion, is described as an additional analysis, uses an unreferenced cut-off, compares two clusters rather than SGDS levels across the cohort, and reports no event counts or adjustment set.

6b. Strategy for model building is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model?
signalling.quote: Significant predictors from univariate analyses were included as covariates in subsequent multivariate Cox regression analyses to evaluate the differences in the risk of progression to AD between resulting subgroups of aMCI patients.

signalling.question: 6c. The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study?
signalling.quote: aMCI participants who did not progress to AD dementia or other dementias.

signalling.question: 6c (additional). Were model assumptions (proportional hazards, linearity of SGDS) checked?
signalling.quote: Searched the Statistical analysis section and Results for a proportional hazards check or any assessment of the functional form of SGDS; the section ends: The analyses were performed using SPSS 28.0.

signalling.question: 6d. There is no selective reporting of results?
signalling.quote: In the present study, because we focused on the presence of MBI domains, the SGDS score was adjusted for multivariate Cox regression analyses. To confirm the effect of severity of depressive symptoms, we additionally dichotomized the affective dysregulation group using the SGDS score.

applicability.rationale: Amnestic MCI patients aged 60 to 85 at two Seoul centres (mean education 8.4 years), restricted to those with more than one year of follow-up and excluding psychiatric illness affecting cognition, which may have removed patients with more severe depression.
The SGDS is a brief, widely used scale and the principal estimate is per point; the > 6 threshold of the sensitivity analysis is unreferenced.
Clinical AD diagnosis by NINCDS-ADRDA (1984) criteria without amyloid or tau biomarkers or neuropathological confirmation.

overall_rationale: Study confounding is high: the principal estimate is univariate, unadjusted for baseline cognition, age, education or co-occurring neuropsychiatric symptoms, the adjusted SGDS estimate is not reported, and APOE and cardiovascular disease were not measured. The other five domains are moderate (eligibility conditioned on follow-up and on the type of dementia reached; unreported exclusions for inadequate follow-up; SGDS administration and completeness undescribed with an unreferenced cut-off; clinical diagnosis at varying intervals with no stated blinding; univariable covariate screening, an omitted adjusted estimate and a post hoc sensitivity analysis). By the QUIPS rule one high domain, or three or more moderate domains, gives high; both conditions are met.
